name: Graft
text:
Decision: We will turn every new piece of information into a short, plain-language sentence that links it to something we already know. For example, if we learn that “sleep helps memory,” we’ll phrase it as “Sleep helps memory the way a nightly backup protects your work—it saves what you learned today so you can use it tomorrow.”

Why this works: It forces us to extract the core meaning and attach it to an existing mental anchor, which builds a stronger brain graph. The trade-off is speed—it takes a few extra seconds per fact—but we gain recall that lasts.
